briefFeedback.deepseek-v4-pro: The exact source snippets and generation history were the most useful; they let me see that `icd_mapper.py` and `icd_mapper_list.py` already handle encodings while `icd_mapper_unique.py` does not, and they warned me away from re-attempting short-row recovery. The limitation of one improvement per generation prevented me from also adding a shared encoding helper across the scripts, which would reduce duplication but would be more than one focus. The frozen tests being append-only is a good backstop, though the measured edge-case names can be slightly misleading because they are not all covered by those tests.
briefFeedback.glm-5.3: The generation history with failure reasons was the most valuable part — it stopped me re-attempting the short-row design that review already rejected three times. The measured dimensions give useful steering. The frozen-tests constraint is reasonable, but the fact that tests only cover `icd_mapper.py` while three sibling scripts share the same fragile reading logic means improvements to the siblings are unverifiable by the gate — I'd let the harness add smoke tests for the other scripts.
briefFeedback.kimi-k3: Genuinely helpful: the non-negotiable constraints made the choice obvious once I noticed a sibling reader violating the spirit of constraint 1; the detailed gen-002 failure record (three rejections with reasons) steered me away from a fourth doomed attempt at short-row recovery; and the source dump preserving trailing whitespace made exact-match edits feasible. Constraining for no good reason: the brief hints "the four scripts duplicate a lot of reading logic" but the editable allowlist is exactly those four files and the "create-only pattern" for new files is referenced yet never defined — so the hinted fix is inexpressible; either define the pattern and bless one helper module, or delete the hint. The dual format requirement (SUMMARY/RATIONALE "exactly this format" vs the PILLAR/PROBLEM/… structure) is contradictory on its face — state explicitly that both are expected. I would delete the "files over 500 lines" metric at this scale (pure noise) and the html code fences around source, which add mismatch paranoia with no benefit.

flagged.notification:
esc-001 — Characterisation tests never assert that a short row is kept, so this recovery can regress without a red build.
Target: pipeline
Raised by: grok-4.6 (xai), generation 002
Agreement: 3 distinct models across 3 labs (xai, deepseek, zai)

The case:
tests/test_icd_mapper.py has no case for a non-blank row with omitted trailing columns. Add one fixture row with <8 fields and assert the ICD-10 code is present via get_mapping. That would lock 8/8 recovery. Risk is low if the fixture only omits trailing empties and expects the same None-for-blank behaviour as test_optional_columns_become_none_when_blank.

Backed by:
  - grok-4.6 (xai, generation 002)
  - deepseek-v4-pro (deepseek, generation 004)
      the characterisation suite has no short-row fixture, so any future short-row recovery can be lost without a red build. Adding a fixture row with fewer than 8 fields and asserting `get_mapping` returns the ICD-10 code would lock the intended 8/8 edge-case behaviour. The risk is low if the row omits only trailing empty columns and expects the same None-for-blank semantics as the existing optional-column test.
  - glm-5.3 (zai, generation 004)
      short-row recovery has been accepted-then-rejected three times precisely because no test pins the intended behaviour; a fixture row with omitted trailing empties plus an assertion via `get_mapping` would settle it.

Argued against by:
  - kimi-k3 (moonshot, generation 004)
      it asks the pipeline to lock short-row recovery (asserting the code is present via get_mapping), but review rejected that recovery three times in gen-002 because a short row cannot be distinguished from one with a genuinely truncated mandatory descriptor; accepting such rows risks silently blanked required fields. The rehearsed, safe behaviour is warn-and-skip, which already satisfies the brief ("reported, not dropped without a word"). Locking "kept" would enshrine behaviour reviewers deemed unsafe; if a test is added, it should assert the warning-and-skip, not the recovery.
